# Study 02, Experiments 0 and 1: review checks (generated by scripts/s2_review.py)

Written in review, after the results were known. Part A re-derives pre-registered quantities and checks the data; Part B is post-hoc and exploratory. No result file of Experiments 0 and 1 is changed.

## Part A. Verification

### A1. Hold-outs and leakage

| split | families | hops | with a held-out test edge | with a held-out test tool | all tools practised | family also in the practice space |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| test_comp | 600 | 2:182/3:206/4:212 | 600 | 0 | 600 | 0 |
| test_depth | 200 | 5:100/6:100 | 0 | 0 | 200 | 0 |
| test_tool | 200 | 1:29/2:55/3:58/4:58 | 0 | 200 | 0 | 0 |
| test_domain | 200 | 1:50/2:54/3:51/4:45 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| test_id | 200 | 1:49/2:51/3:50/4:50 | 0 | 0 | 200 | 200 |

Practice families that contain a held-out edge or tool: 0 of 5364. `dev` families that touch a test hold-out: 0. **Pass.** `test_id` is drawn from the practice space by design (see B1).

### A2. Training subsets

- 20 subsets rebuilt from the practice space: nested within a replicate (True), and identical in family list, tool coverage and edge coverage to `results/study02/e1/training_sets.json` (True).
- 20 training sets rebuilt on CPU (3,200 oracle episodes each): SHA-256 equal to the run config and to the hash each GPU job recorded (True).
- Two replicates share 776-805 of their 1,600 families, so replicates are separate draws from one practice space, not disjoint sets.

### A3. What was scored (episodes per run and split)

| runs | own | dev | test_id | test_comp | test_depth | test_tool | test_domain | eval_id | eval_ood | eval_unseen | eval_renamed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5B, 20 trained runs | 400 | 600 | 400 | 1200 | 400 | 400 | 400 | 200 | 240 | 120 | 160 |

Every cell is either the full split or empty: no partial split entered a table. The 1.5B student has no `dev`, `test_depth`, `test_tool` or `test_domain` rows, and the baselines have no anchor or secondary-test rows. No run has a duplicated episode.

### A5. The confirmatory contrast, derived a second time

| student | D = 1,600 minus D = 25, per replicate | Student-t interval over replicates | bootstrap written here (replicates, families, tasks) | interval in `e1/summary.json` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5B | +18.3, +16.2, +18.1, +18.7, +22.9 | +18.8 [+15.8, +21.9] | [+15.7, +22.3] | +18.9 [+15.7, +22.2] |
| 1.5B | +30.0, +23.0, +27.6 | +26.9 [+18.0, +35.7] | [+22.3, +31.4] | +26.9 [+22.2, +31.4] |

H1 is supported for both students under either interval. With three replicates the percentile bootstrap is too narrow for the 1.5B student; the Student-t interval (+26.9 [+18.0, +35.7]) is the one to quote. The 0.5B ceiling at D = 1,600 is 37.7 [34.0, 41.4] by the same method: the point estimate is below 40% and the interval includes it.

### A6. Cost

51 jobs in the ledger, 6 ended in error, total billed 50.37 USD of the 60 USD cap.
2 jobs were billed more than the launcher had reserved for them (`e1_s05_D100_r0_score` by 0.0167 USD, `e1_s05_D100_r3_score` by 0.0167 USD): both ran into their time limit, and the provider bills two minutes beyond a time limit where the launcher reserved one. The 3 USD reserve absorbed it and the cap held, but the launcher's claim that a job cannot cost more than its reservation was not true. Fixed in review (`reservation_usd`).

### A7. List selections re-derived from the task worlds

The reference-model gate vouched for families of at most two hops. This check covers the property it was meant to protect at every depth: for each gold call that lists records, the selection rule is read back from the request text and applied to the task's world, and must single out exactly one record, the one the gold graph or the answer then uses. It shares the phrase templates with the generator and nothing else.

| tasks | checked | selections | not applicable (graph stops before selecting) | failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| test_comp | 1200 | 1992 | 0 | 0 |
| test_depth | 400 | 1120 | 0 | 0 |
| test_tool | 384 | 590 | 16 | 0 |
| test_domain | 382 | 424 | 18 | 0 |
| test_id | 390 | 530 | 10 | 0 |
| dev | 590 | 780 | 10 | 0 |
| practice (2 training instances per family) | 10360 | 20204 | 368 | 0 |

**Pass.** This does not test whether a request reads naturally or whether a model would find it clear; it tests that the stated rule has one answer in the world and that the gold graph follows it.

## Part B. Post-hoc analyses (chosen in review; exploratory)

### B1. `test_id` mixes practised and unpractised families

`test_id` holds 200 families of the practice space. A run's training subset contains some of them, and the share grows with D, so the rise of `test_id` with D mixes two things: generalisation to unpractised families built from practised edges, and more of the split being practised.

| student | D | `test_id` families in the run's training subset | success, in subset | success, not in subset |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5B | 25 | 1% | 62.5 | 30.6 |
| 0.5B | 100 | 4% | 69.8 | 44.9 |
| 0.5B | 400 | 15% | 67.8 | 44.8 |
| 0.5B | 1600 | 57% | 63.6 | 34.2 |
| 1.5B | 25 | 1% | 87.5 | 63.2 |
| 1.5B | 1600 | 57% | 87.4 | 73.7 |

The two groups differ in depth (shallow families are over-represented among the practised ones), so the columns are not a like-for-like contrast; B2 gives that. Where the report calls `test_id` "practised families", read "families of the practice space".

### B2. In-distribution accuracy and the number of families

Own-family success per replicate, and differences paired on replicate (Student-t interval). The last column scores the same tasks at both levels: the own-family tasks that both runs were given, which are instances of the families the smaller training subset contains.

| student | contrast | own-family success, all tasks | on identical tasks |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5B | D = 100 minus D = 25 | -9.9 [-11.9, -8.0] | -11.2 [-17.5, -4.9] (100 tasks per replicate) |
| 0.5B | D = 1,600 minus D = 100 | -1.1 [-5.1, +2.8] | +4.8 [-0.1, +9.7] (100 tasks per replicate) |
| 0.5B | D = 1,600 minus D = 25 | -11.1 [-14.3, -7.9] | -10.4 [-22.9, +2.1] (25 tasks per replicate) |
| 1.5B | D = 1,600 minus D = 25 | -2.4 [-4.9, +0.1] | -1.3 [-7.1, +4.4] (25 tasks per replicate) |

The identical tasks of the widest contrast by number of hops, replicates pooled (success % at 25 and at 1,600 families; few tasks per cell): 0.5B: 1 hops 80 to 90 (n = 20), 2 hops 77 to 74 (n = 35), 3 hops 63 to 37 (n = 35), 4 hops 46 to 31 (n = 35); 1.5B: 1 hops 92 to 100 (n = 12), 2 hops 90 to 95 (n = 21), 3 hops 95 to 90 (n = 21), 4 hops 90 to 81 (n = 21).

For the 0.5B student the fall is real and is confined to the first step: 62.5% at 25 families (128 instances each), 52.5% at 100 (32 each), 50.0% and 51.4% at 400 and 1,600 (8 and 2 each). What is lost is the benefit of seeing one family more than a hundred times, not accuracy that keeps eroding as families are added. The 1.5B student shows no reliable fall.

### B3. `test_comp` tasks that no trained run solved

The report counts families: 3 of 600 were never solved. Counting tasks, 74 of 1200 were never solved in 26 attempts (by hops: 2: 15, 3: 11, 4: 48). They follow the number of list selections a request makes ("the order with the lowest total among..."), which the hop count does not capture:

| list selections in the request | tasks | never solved | 0.5B, D = 1,600 | 1.5B, D = 1,600 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 116 | 2 | 82.2 | 92.2 |
| 1 | 416 | 8 | 51.2 | 87.3 |
| 2 | 464 | 32 | 25.4 | 71.9 |
| 3 | 168 | 24 | 14.2 | 60.5 |
| 4 | 36 | 8 | 5.6 | 47.2 |

All 26 never-solved tasks of at most three hops were read in review with their oracle transcripts. Each has one defensible reading and a correct gold answer; they are hard because they chain two to four selections or need a weekday turned into a date. This is a check by reading, on a sample chosen by difficulty. It does not replace the reference-model gate for deep families.

### B4. The eight-turn limit and `test_depth`

The runtime, reused unchanged from Study 01, ends an episode after eight turns. On `test_depth` the oracle itself needs 6 turns on 36% of tasks, 7 turns on 50% of tasks, 8 turns on 14% of tasks. A six-hop task with a retry therefore fails after a single wasted turn.

| split | student | D = 25 | D = 100 | D = 400 | D = 1600 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| test_depth, episodes ended by the limit (%) | 0.5B | 35.4 | 32.2 | 22.3 | 20.0 |
| test_comp, episodes ended by the limit (%) | 0.5B | 14.7 | 10.2 | 3.9 | 3.2 |
| test_comp, episodes ended by the limit (%) | 1.5B | 3.3 | - | - | 0.3 |

`test_depth` is near the floor partly for this reason, and the report should say so. The limit does not explain the four-hop results on the primary endpoint, where the oracle needs at most six turns.

### B5. How four-hop `test_comp` episodes fail at D = 1,600

| student | success | answered before the minimum number of turns | failures missing a required call | failures with an invented tool | failures ended by a limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5B | 19.4 | 42.4 | 93.7 | 8.0 | 9.1 |
| 1.5B | 66.0 | 20.4 | 90.5 | 2.8 | 1.9 |

Failures are wrong or missing calls and early answers, the errors of a model that loses the chain. No episode comes near the 256-token limit per turn (longest mean: 125 tokens), so truncation is not a cause.

### B6. The reference model by depth (first attempts, `Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct`, few-shot)

| hops | tasks | solved | mean turns used | minimum turns needed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 128 | 82.8 | 2.4 | 2.2 |
| 2 | 342 | 35.4 | 3.0 | 3.3 |
| 4 | 200 | 3.0 | 3.0 | 5.3 |

The reference model is competent at one hop only. At four hops it stops after three turns on average where five are the minimum, so its failures say nothing about the tasks. Three-, five- and six-hop test families were not attempted by it at all, and four-hop ones only in the run that was stopped. A trained 1.5B student solves 66.0% of four-hop `test_comp` tasks and is the better reference (see the Experiment 2 plan).
